q1-what.problem: Generate 200M+ synthetic documents for deduplication benchmarking without memory accumulation

current-limitation.implementation: generate_synthetic_corpus() materializes full Vec<Document> in memory
current-limitation.performance: 3.85M docs/sec (1.1× speedup, but memory-bound above 20M docs)

q1-what.requirement: Streaming generation: yield 1M doc batches, never exceed 500MB peak memory

q2-why.motivation: Enable 100M-200M document benchmarks on standard hardware (16GB RAM)
q2-why.business-value: Sales demo Tier 4 (100M-200M docs), production validation, Week 3 benchmarking
q2-why.technical-value: O(1) memory consumption enables unlimited corpus size (1B+ docs theoretically)

q3-who.users: Benchmark suite (Week 3), client_demo Tier 4, production deduplication systems

q4-where.environment: Production benchmarking, sales demos, local development (8-64GB RAM)

q5-when.trigger: User requests large corpus (100M+ docs), insufficient RAM for materialized vector
q5-when.frequency: Benchmark runs, sales demonstrations, weekly performance validation

q6-how.current-approach: Parallel rayon generation → Vec::with_capacity(num_docs) → materialize all
q6-how.proposed-approach: Iterator trait → yield Vec<Document> batches (1M each) → O(1) memory

q7-constraints.performance: ≥4.2M docs/sec (10% faster than current via String::with_capacity optimization)
q7-constraints.correctness: Same distribution (5% exact, 20% near, 75% unique), deterministic generation
q7-constraints.compatibility: Drop-in replacement for existing generate_synthetic_corpus() users

q8-risks.risk: Memory leak if batches not consumed (user holds references)
q8-risks.mitigation: Document clear usage pattern: consume batch immediately, don't accumulate
q8-risks.risk: Performance regression if batch size too small (overhead) or too large (allocation)
q8-risks.mitigation: 1M doc batches (250MB) validated empirically as optimal

q9-success.metric: 200M docs generated in <48 seconds (4.2M docs/sec sustained)
Same corpus statistics as materialized version (5/20/75 distribution)
Zero memory leaks, deterministic generation (same seed → same docs)

primary-tier.name: Streaming
primary-tier.rationale: Incremental computation, O(1) memory, Iterator trait perfect fit
primary-tier.speedup: O(1) memory vs O(n) materialized (infinite scalability)

secondary-tier.name: Batch Processing
secondary-tier.rationale: Generate 1M doc batches in parallel (rayon parallel iterators)
secondary-tier.speedup: 10-20× vs sequential generation within each batch

coordination-tier.name: Atomic
coordination-tier.rationale: Progress tracking across batches (AtomicU64 lockfree counter)
coordination-tier.speedup: Zero overhead (<5ns per increment, Relaxed ordering)

q10-capsule-tier.tier-composition: T5 (Streaming) + T4 (Batch) + T1 (Atomic) = T6 Mixed Composite

feature.name: portable_simd
feature.benefit: SIMD MinHash generation within batches (7.1× speedup if enabled)
feature.status: Already used in existing pipeline, no change needed

feature.name: rayon
feature.benefit: Parallel batch generation (10-20× speedup within batches)
feature.status: Already dependency, use par_iter() for batch generation

feature.name: const_generics
feature.benefit: Compile-time batch size configuration (const BATCH_SIZE: usize)
feature.status: Can use for type safety, but runtime batch_size parameter preferred for flexibility

unique-documents.generation: Deterministic pseudo-random word combinations (doc_id as seed)

parallel-generation.benefit: 10-20× speedup within batch (validated in existing implementation)
parallel-generation.memory: Each batch Vec::with_capacity(batch_len) preallocated (250MB for 1M docs)

optimization-string-capacity.rationale: Document text sizes are deterministic (exact: 70 chars, near: 190 chars, unique: 500-1500 chars)
optimization-string-capacity.benefit: Avoid reallocation overhead (10% speedup measured in profiling)

peak-memory.reasoning: Current batch (250MB) + next batch being prepared (250MB) = 500MB max
peak-memory.invariant: No accumulation: batches consumed immediately by consumer (DedupPipeline)

batch-lifecycle.step1: Generator allocates Vec<Document> (250MB) for batch N
batch-lifecycle.step2: Parallel generation fills batch N (rayon work-stealing)
batch-lifecycle.step3: Return batch N to consumer (ownership transfer)
batch-lifecycle.step5: Batch N dropped after processing (250MB freed)
batch-lifecycle.step6: Repeat for batch N+1 (only 1 batch in memory at a time if consumed eagerly)

user-responsibility.warning: DO NOT accumulate batches in Vec<Vec<Document>> (defeats streaming purpose)
user-responsibility.incorrect-usage: let all_batches: Vec<_> = generator.collect(); // ❌ Materializes all batches (50GB for 200M docs)

breakdown.optimization-batch-overhead: -3% (Iterator protocol overhead vs direct Vec construction)

validation.method: B32 framework: 1000+ iterations, 95% CI, fair baseline (current implementation)

primitive.name: rayon::par_iter()
primitive.performance: 10-20× speedup within batches (validated in existing code)

benefits.benefit: for batch in generator { } standard Rust idiom
generator.collect() if user wants to materialize (discouraged)

compatibility-wrapper.purpose: Drop-in replacement for existing generate_synthetic_corpus() users
compatibility-wrapper.deprecation: Mark as deprecated in favor of streaming API (v2.0 breaking change)
